subject: Territorial anchoring: ephemeral cross-hop window and subprocessor roster review
messages:
From: Alice Walker <alice.walker@atlas.health>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: Atlas Legal <legal@atlas.health>
Date: Wed, 28 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ephemeral cross-hop processing — need subprocessor roster & constraints

Sean —

Quick intro: I’m Alice (Data Privacy lead at Atlas Health). We’re close to a security review for our pilot using Redwood for embeddings + inference. A few items we need to validate before Legal will sign off on the DPA addendum:

- Exact list of subprocessors that could touch customer data during a conditional or temporary cross-region processing event (we call this an "ephemeral cross-hop").
- Maximum duration Redwood will allow for transient processing outside the customer’s territory (if any).
- Whether data remains encrypted in transit/at-rest during such a hop and which KMS/HSM controls apply.
- What audit evidence you can provide (eg. egress event logs, timestamps, and proof of deletion).

We have some hard constraints: no processing outside the US/EEA/APAC for longer than 96 hours without prior approval, SOC2 evidence for any new subprocessor, and DPA language covering short-term failover.

Can you share the roster and a short description of your operational guardrails? We are trying to keep this tight (legal is firm on timeboxes).

Thanks,
Alice Walker
Data Privacy Manager
Atlas Health

Attachment: atlas_soc2_evidence_request.pdf (pdf stub)
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Alice Walker <alice.walker@atlas.health>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 May 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ephemeral cross-hop processing — need subprocessor roster & constraints

Alice —

Thanks for the clear ask and context. Short answer up front: Redwood supports a constrained, auditable transient processing window for failover and burst scenarios (we don’t call it routine routing). Below are the operational guardrails we propose for Atlas to include in the DPA addendum; I’ve attached the current subprocessor roster and a draft DPA addendum for your review.

Key points:
- Transient processing window: default maximum 72 hours for any ephemeral cross-hop without written exec approval. This is configurable per-customer in enterprise contracts but 72h is our standard safety cap.
- Encryption: data remains encrypted in transit (TLS1.3) and at-rest. When ephemeral hops occur, data is processed in memory on a short-lived instance. Customer-managed KMS is supported for keys-in-use; where customer KMS is not configured, we use customer-specific envelope keys stored in our HSM-backed key store.
- Subprocessors: attached roster includes compute, telemetry, and storage subprocessors. Any new subprocessor that may be involved in a transient hop requires SOC2 Type II evidence (or equivalent) prior to activation for your account.
- Auditability: egress events are written to a tamper-evident audit log (timestamp, source region, destination region, duration, request ids). We can provide CSV extracts for the event window on request.
- Deletion & retention: ephemeral copies are garbage-collected immediately after the processing job completes; retention for transient artifacts is 0–24 hours depending on in-flight batching. We can add a DPA clause to limit residual artifacts to 24 hours max.

Attachments included: redwood_subprocessors_roster_v2.xlsx, DPA-addendum-draft.docx, ephemeral-egress-runbook.pdf (runbook is an ops-level summary of how the window is triggered and monitored).

Next steps I propose:
1) Legal reviews the DPA addendum draft and highlights any non-starters.
2) Marissa (cc’d) will verify runbook-level controls and confirm whether the 72h cap is operationally feasible across our regions.
3) If Atlas requires a shorter cap, we’ll scope an ops implementation plan and timeline.

Happy to jump on a quick call this week to walk through the runbook.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Enterprise Sales (East)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Ephemeral cross-hop processing — need subprocessor roster & constraints

Looping in operational details below so Alice and Legal have a concrete picture of risk/impact. Quoting Sean's note above.

Operational clarifications (ops perspective):
- Triggering: ephemeral cross-hop is only triggered by policy (region capacity, degraded availability) or explicit customer request (failover). It is not used for normal routing.
- Max duration: 72h is fine as a contractual cap. Practically, we aim to close events <24h for burst scenarios; multi-day incidents require an incident response plan and customer consent.
- Telemetry & latency: ephemeral hops do not change our inference model execution path; however, for telemetry capture we temporarily persist KV cache snapshots to encrypted ephemeral storage which can add 30–120ms to tail latency for affected requests during the warm-up window. We log this in the audit event.
- Audit evidence: we can provide a per-event package: egress log CSV, instance IDs, transitive-region mapping, and a hash-based proof of deletion after GC. We retain these proof artifacts for 90 days for audit purposes.
- Subprocessor activation: we run a staged onboarding for any subprocessor that will see customer data — SOC2 evidence collection -> legal attestation -> technical gating. For Atlas we recommend pre-approval of the current roster and a clause that requires 10 business days notice for adding a new subprocessor that might be used in an ephemeral hop.

I’ve attached the ephemeral-egress-runbook.pdf for your review (it includes the step-by-step event lifecycle and notification hooks to customers).

If Atlas wants a shorter contractual cap (48h or less), we’ll need to update our operational runbook and CI templates; that would be a ~3-week ops change to hard-enforce via policy. If acceptable from your side, we can scope that as a one-off addendum.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks Sean and Marissa — this is very helpful. A few quick notes from Legal and Privacy: 

- The 72h default cap is acceptable as long as the DPA addendum includes a notification requirement within 1 hour of any ephemeral hop and a mandatory post-event package (egress CSV + deletion proof).
- We need SOC2 evidence for all subprocessors listed that could be used in the hop; Atlas Legal will review the roster and confirm any items that need deeper vetting.
- Requesting the DPA addendum be updated to include: (1) 1-hour notification SLA for ephemeral hops, (2) 24-hour maximum retention for transient artifacts unless otherwise consented, and (3) a 10-business-day notice period for onboarding any new subprocessor that may participate in ephemeral hops.

If you can send an updated DPA that reflects those three bullets, we’ll circulate internally and send a DocuSign link. We’ve attached a short checklist (atlas_soc2_evidence_request.pdf) that lists the specific artifacts our procurement team will require; can you confirm which you can deliver as part of the initial onboarding?

Assuming we get the DPA updated, Atlas is ok to proceed to a short pilot restricted to US-region workloads with the transient hop guardrails in place.

Best,
Alice Walker
Data Privacy Manager
Atlas Health
